recognize_zh: 箭頭指的細胞有圓形、未分葉的核，胞質被粗大、大小一致的顆粒填滿並蓋到核上，這是嗜酸性骨髓球（eosinophilic myelocyte）；早期嗜酸性顆粒常偏紫深色，易被誤認為嗜鹼性球，下方可見顆粒偏橘紅的較成熟嗜酸性細胞作對照。
features: Arrowed cell with a round to oval, non-lobated nucleus and moderately condensed chromatin
Cytoplasm packed with coarse, uniform, round granules that appear dark purple-brown (immature eosinophilic granules)
Granules evenly distributed, extending to the cell margin
Adjacent larger precursor with fine chromatin and pale blue cytoplasm (promyelocyte/early precursor)
Nearby eosinophilic precursor with coarse orange-red granules for comparison; marrow aspirate background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows an eosinophilic myelocyte (arrow) with a round, non-lobated nucleus and cytoplasm filled with coarse uniform granules, some of which have a darker, basophilic hue typical of immature eosinophil granules. An adjacent early myeloid precursor and a more mature eosinophilic cell with orange-red granules are present for comparison. The granules are round and uniform rather than irregular and water-soluble. Findings represent a normal eosinophilic myelocyte.

ddx.vs: Basophil granules are fewer, irregular, deep purple-black, obscure the nucleus, and are often partially dissolved, while eosinophil granules are uniform and round with an orange tint when mature.
Neutrophilic myelocytes have fine lilac specific granules with a paranuclear clear zone, not coarse refractile granules filling the cytoplasm.

ddx.dx: Abnormal eosinophils in AML with inv(16)
ddx.vs: Inv(16) eosinophils show large, dark basophilic-staining granules admixed with eosinophilic ones in immature cells, together with increased blasts.
Mast cells are larger with an oval central nucleus and dense purple metachromatic granules, often spindle-shaped, and are tryptase and CD117 positive.
